justification: B fits the content in four pages with well-filled pages and running header/footer bands that give section context and page counts. A ends with a mostly empty page (A5) and leaves a large gap at the bottom of A3. A's serif text is elegant and readable. B's sans text is equally clear, and its pagination and rhythm are tighter overall.

A runs its sections continuously with consistent headings and thin rules, so the pages flow evenly. Its one flaw is the Functions intro on A5, which is set in a larger, inconsistent body size. B breaks the flow in several places. It inserts a lone chapter divider for History only (B5), which disrupts the rhythm. It strands the Etymology image with a half-empty page beneath it (B4). Its justified text leaves wide word gaps in the ISO list (B8). Its heavy header and footer bands add clutter. B's section numbering is a minor plus.

B's serif body text with numbered bold headings reads more comfortably and gives clearer hierarchy. A's light 'Potential' and 'Thermal energy' heads are weaker than its bold subheads (A2, A4). B's text flows continuously and fills its pages better. In A, page 3 is half empty and the map sits alone with a large blank area (A3, A6). B places the map after its text (B6). A's navy cover and header bands are more striking, but the dense sans body with heavy hyphenation is less pleasant to read.

A strands images and short sections on near-empty pages: A5 is just one photo above a blank page, and A3 and A8 are mostly empty. Its section titles hang left of the text column, and the drop caps are inconsistent. B flows content continuously with images inline, so its pages are well filled (B3, B4). It also adds clean header and footer bands. B's light-weight H2 headings are slightly weaker, but overall pacing is much better.

A runs text and images in a steady flow, with consistent header and footer bands and well-filled pages. B strands the Ashurbanipal image alone on a mostly empty page (B5) and leaves large voids below the content on B3, B4 and B8. B also hangs its headings in the left margin and gives the Functions lead paragraph an inconsistent larger size (B6), so its rhythm is uneven.

A takes 7 pages to B's 6. Its image page A4 is mostly empty, and A5 opens with a large blank top. A also has drop caps and stronger bold headings. B packs the content more continuously: the image shares a page with the Thermal energy section on B4. Its consistent header and footer bands give structure. Its light-weight H1 headings are weaker than A's bold ones, but B's page use and flow are clearly better.

A strands the photo on a nearly empty page (A4) and the map with a large void below (A7), and it pushes Thermal energy to a new page with big gaps (A5). B flows the image directly into the next section (B4) and fits the content into 6 continuous pages with consistent running headers. A's blue cover and drop caps add some character, but the broken flow and wasted space outweigh them.

A has a numbered TOC and heavy navy header/footer bands with a mid-document section divider (A5) that only appears for History, an inconsistent break, plus half-empty pages (A4, A7) that make the flow choppy. B runs sections continuously with consistent rules and headings, filling pages evenly (B4–B7). However, B's Functions intro on B5 suddenly switches to a larger, ragged-right style. A's serif with tight justification also produces stretched word spacing on A8, which is a minor flaw.

A sets the text in a classic serif with generous leading and adds a table of contents. B uses a light sans-serif with tight justification and visible word gaps (B5, B6), and its heavy header and footer bands crowd the pages. A has one flaw: the Functions intro on A5 is set at a larger size, which is inconsistent. Overall, A reads more comfortably.

A pairs a serif body with sans headings, giving more comfortable reading text, and its sections start on fresh pages. This leaves A5 half-empty, but the pages feel calm. B is denser and runs continuously. Its light sans body with wide measure is tiring to read, sections such as Antiquity split across pages B2–B3, and the running headers mislabel content.

A fits the content in four pages with consistent fill and running headers that show the current section. B's serif setting is elegant, but it leaves a mostly empty final page (B5) with only a short paragraph. Its header bands carry no labels. A's top and bottom bands are heavier but give useful navigation.

A keeps a consistent header/footer band, a TOC, and the History image sitting with its text on A6. B strands the Ashurbanipal image alone on a mostly empty B5. B's headings hang outdented and its drop caps break line spacing on B4, B6 and B8. B6 also shifts between larger and smaller body text inconsistently. A's section divider on A5 is somewhat wasteful, but A reads more evenly overall.

B's serif body text sets a more comfortable reading line, and its numbered headings, table of contents and History divider give clearer structure. A is more compact but uses a light sans body with wide measure, and its section heads are inconsistent: thin heads on A3–A4, bold heads on A5–A6. B's costs are the half-empty Etymology page (B4) and a mostly blank divider (B5), so A packs space better.

A sets a consistent serif text with even justification and a steady rhythm; its only weakness is a near-empty final page (A5). B's drop caps are oddly placed and leave paragraphs ragged and unjustified (B3, B4, B5). B's justification also shows loose word spacing, and its page breaks leave uneven gaps (B2). On balance, A reads more cleanly.

A pairs serif body text with a bold sans for headings, using generous margins and clear numbered headings. This gives a calm, readable page. B's body text is wider and denser, and its main section heads (Potential, Thermal energy) are set in a light weight. That makes them weaker than the bold subheads beneath them, which muddles the hierarchy. B's dark cover and heavy header and footer bands are striking, but the inner pages read less comfortably.

A pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body and has more generous leading, so the section structure is easy to scan. Its drop caps add some interest, though they are inconsistent: they appear on some sections only, and the text beside them loses justification (A3, A5). B uses a uniform serif with tighter, wider lines that read denser. B's headings are less distinct, and its running header is just 'Bridge' (B2-B4). B's top rule bands are tidy, but its last page is nearly empty (B5).

Design A pairs serif body text with sans headings, adds a table of contents, numbered sections and a strong chapter divider band. This gives clearer navigation and a calmer reading texture. Its weak points are a near-empty divider page and loose page breaks with underfilled pages (A4, A5). Design B is more compact and continuous but has weaker structure. Its light grotesque body is harder to read at length, and its headings are thin and understated, so section breaks get lost (B3, B4).

A uses a sans heading face with a serif body, which gives clear contrast, and its numbered sections are easy to find. Its pages break more cleanly, so no page ends almost empty. B's EB Garamond body is set small and dense on a wide measure, and its headings stand out less. B also ends on a near-empty page with only seven lines (B5). A's header and footer bands carry running section titles, which helps navigation.

A pairs a serif text face with sans headings and uses drop caps, giving clearer section openings and a more bookish read with generous margins (A3, A4). However, its drop-cap paragraphs switch to ragged, unjustified text, which is inconsistent (A3, A5), and page 5 is left largely empty. B is denser and uniform. Its header and footer bands frame the pages well (B2–B4), but the running header on B2 says 'Antiquity' before that section starts, and the tight sans text with small headings feels cramped. Overall, A reads more comfortably.

A integrates the photo with the Thermal energy section on A4 and keeps text flowing, with only a half-empty page before the figure. B isolates the photo on B4, leaving most of the page blank, then starts B5 with a large empty top band. That breaks the reading flow. B's blue cover and drop caps add some character, but the stranded image pages and wasted space hurt rhythm and balance.

A sets an elegant serif in a wide, evenly filled measure, so the text runs continuously and only the last page is short (A5). B's text is narrower and its justification opens wide gaps between words (B5). B also breaks sections early, leaving large empty areas at the foot of B2 and B3. Its heavy dark header and footer bars crowd the page (B2–B5). B's numbered sans headings and running section titles help navigation slightly, but A reads more calmly overall.

The two designs share the same content and cover style. A uses drop caps on some sections but not others (A3, A4, A5), and the paragraphs beside them are ragged-right and unjustified, unlike the rest of the text. That makes the pages look patchy. A4's running footer reads "1400 to 1750" while the page continues into a later section. B keeps paragraph styling consistent and numbers its sections. Its slim header and footer bands give clear orientation (B2–B5), though they are a little heavy. B's sections also break more cleanly at page boundaries.

B's serif text face sets more comfortably, with lighter and more generous measure. It adds a table of contents (B2) and a calm thin top rule. A's heavy navy header and footer bands (A2–A6) give running section labels. However, its dense grotesque body text and the size mismatch between its light H2s and bold H3s (A3, A5) read less refined. B has one flaw: the Functions paragraph on B5 jumps to a larger size.

A is quieter and more consistent: light running footers, a clear section rule and heading treatment, and drop caps. Its weak spots are image pages that strand on A5 and short sections on A8. B adds a TOC, but the heavy dark header and footer bars crowd every page. The B5 chapter-divider spread is used only once, for History, so it breaks rhythm and leaves an awkward near-empty page. B's thin-weight '1 Etymology' and '3 Functions' headings also look inconsistent with its bold '3.1' heading. B does pair the History image with its text on B6, which is a plus.

B sets the text in a serif with wider margins and shorter lines, so the long body copy reads more comfortably. Its numbered headings give clearer structure. A's sans body runs wide and dense across nearly full-width pages. B has a large empty bottom on B5, and A is more compact. Even so, B reads better overall.

A flows consistently: the figures sit inline with the text, sections follow each other naturally, and it includes a table of contents. B strands the Ashurbanipal image alone on a mostly blank page (B5) and leaves large voids on B3 and B4. B's headings hang outdented past the text column, its drop caps are inconsistent, and its body text is letterspaced and uneven, with one oversized lead paragraph on B6. A's larger lead paragraph on A5 is a minor flaw by comparison.

A keeps a consistent, justified serif body with clear numbered headings. Its header and footer bands frame each page cleanly. B's drop caps switch the paragraph into ragged-right text with different spacing, which looks inconsistent (B3, B4, B5). B4's running footer reads '1400 to 1750' while the page continues into 1750 to 1900, and B's light footers are weaker. A's dark bands are slightly heavy, but A's rhythm is more even overall.

B's serif text in a narrower measure with generous margins reads more comfortably than A's wide, dense sans-serif blocks, and its drop caps add rhythm, even though the drop-cap paragraphs ragged-right inconsistently. A's dark header/footer bands look polished but crowd the pages, and on A3–A4 sections run tightly together. B leaves large empty areas on B2 and B5, yet overall it feels calmer and more book-like.

A strands its Ashurbanipal image on an otherwise empty page (A5) and leaves large voids on A3, A4 and A8, which gives it a choppy rhythm. Its headings hang out of line with the body, and the drop caps are applied inconsistently. B flows continuously, places its images inline with the text (B4, B5), and adds a table of contents (B2). Its consistent serif typography and header rule make the pages feel more cohesive.

A places the space photo together with the Thermal energy text on A4, so the page is well filled. B strands the same image on B4, leaving most of the page empty. B5 then opens with an awkward blank band above its heading. B's serif body, drop caps and hanging headings are attractive, but the wasted pages and choppier flow give A the edge.
